title: Injectivity from the closed fibre over a valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, meaning an integral domain for which each nonzero element $a$ of its fraction field satisfies $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$. Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$), essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Let $N,M$ be finite $B$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $u:N\to M$ a $B$-linear map. Suppose $M$, with scalars restricted to $A$, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that the induced map $N/\mathfrak m_AN\to M/\mathfrak m_AM$ is injective, where $\mathfrak m_AN$ and $\mathfrak m_AM$ denote the submodules generated by products of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ with module elements. Then $u$ is injective and the $A$-module $M/u(N)$ is flat.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] there are a finite type $A$-algebra $C$, a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq C$ and an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $B\cong W^{-1}C$, and by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] a surjection of $A$-algebras $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow C$. Let $\rho:P\to C\to W^{-1}C\cong B$ be the composite and $\mathfrak q=\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$, a prime of $P$. Every $p\in P\setminus\mathfrak q$ maps outside $\mathfrak m_B$, hence to a unit of the local ring $B$, so $\rho$ factors through an $A$-algebra map $\pi:P_{\mathfrak q}\to B$. It is surjective: an element of $B$ is $c/w$ with $c=\bar p$, $w=\bar s$ for some $p,s\in P$; since $w/1$ is a unit of $W^{-1}C$, $\rho(s)\notin\mathfrak m_B$, i.e. $s\notin\mathfrak q$, and $c/w=\pi(p/s)$. Since $\pi$ is a surjection of local rings, $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$ is a proper ideal with residue field $B/\mathfrak m_B$, hence the maximal ideal of $P_{\mathfrak q}$; as $A\to B$ is local, the composite $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}\to B$ shows that $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is local. The map $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is essentially of finite presentation (a localization of a finitely presented $A$-algebra) because $P$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] (presentation with $m=0$) and $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is its localization at $P\setminus\mathfrak q$. Regard $N$, $M$, and $u$ as finite $P_{\mathfrak q}$-modules and a $P_{\mathfrak q}$-linear map through $\pi$; the hypotheses (finiteness, flatness of $M$ over $A$, injectivity of the closed-fibre map, which only involves $\mathfrak m_A$) and the conclusions are unchanged because the underlying $A$-modules and the map are unchanged, so it suffices to prove the result with $B$ replaced by $P_{\mathfrak q}$.

Apply [lem-trf-valuation-finite-module-fp-reduction] with the base ring still $A$ and the new local algebra $P_{\mathfrak q}$. We obtain a filtered system of finitely presented $P_{\mathfrak q}$-modules $N_\lambda$ with surjective transition maps, colimit $N$, and, for sufficiently large $\lambda$, an isomorphism $N_\lambda/\mathfrak m_A N_\lambda\cong N/\mathfrak m_A N$. For such a $\lambda$, let $\pi_\lambda:N_\lambda\twoheadrightarrow N$ be the colimit map and set $u_\lambda=u\circ\pi_\lambda:N_\lambda\to M$. The fibre map of $u_\lambda$ is injective because the displayed isomorphism identifies it with the assumed injective fibre map of $u$.
By [lem-trf-valuation-flat-finite-module-presentation], applied to $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ and the finite flat target $M$, the $P_{\mathfrak q}$-module $M$ is finitely presented.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-general-mod-injective] with $R=A$, $S=P_{\mathfrak q}$, source module $M=N_\lambda$, target module $N=M$, and map $u_\lambda$. Step 1 gives that $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is local and essentially of finite presentation; Step 2 gives the finitely presented source and injective closed-fibre map; Step 3 gives the finitely presented target; and the target is flat over $A$ by the hypothesis. The helper therefore gives that $u_\lambda$ is injective and that $M/u_\lambda(N_\lambda)$ is flat over $A$.

proof.text: The map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective and $u_\lambda=u\circ\pi_\lambda$. Since $u_\lambda$ is injective, $\ker(\pi_\lambda)\subseteq\ker(u_\lambda)=0$, so $\pi_\lambda$ is an isomorphism. Under this identification $u=u_\lambda$, and the flatness of $M/u_\lambda(N_\lambda)$ from Step 4 is the flatness of $M/u(N)$.
